auth_observations: Most core market data APIs under https://api.nasdaq.com/api/* are accessed with anonymous GET requests using only standard browser headers and a large cookie jar; no Authorization or CSRF headers are present.

A dedicated clickstream analytics endpoint at https://www.nasdaq.com/ai-search/external/indexer-api/clickstream/publish uses an Authorization: Bearer <JWT> header, indicating an internal service token for indexing/AI search rather than end-user auth.

Extensive use of cookies for tracking, personalization, and consent (Adobe Experience Cloud IDs, Marketo _mkto_trk, OneTrust OptanonConsent, analytics cookies like _ga, _fbp, _uetsid) but none function as explicit API auth tokens for market data.

No evidence of CSRF tokens or custom API keys in headers for api.nasdaq.com calls; access control for these endpoints appears to rely on public/unauthenticated read access with possible server-side rate limiting.
Qualtrics and other third-party analytics/UX tools rely on cookies and their own session identifiers but do not expose additional auth schemes in this capture.
narrative:
This capture contains 452 total requests across 160 unique URLs and 20 hosts. Roughly 240 requests are clear noise or analytics (Google CCM, Bing, Adobe/Marketo/Qualtrics beacons, Reddit/LinkedIn pixels, JWPlayer telemetry, Akamai RUM, etc.), leaving around ~210 requests that contribute to page rendering or core market data.

The main business API surface is on api.nasdaq.com under the /api/ path. Within that, the highest-volume and most central endpoint for the observed task (viewing AAPL and COMP data, including historical series) is GET /api/quote/AAPL/info (24 hits), which provides detailed instrument metadata for AAPL stock. Closely related core endpoints include:
- GET /api/quote/AAPL/summary (summary quote and key stats)
- GET /api/quote/AAPL/chart (time-series chart data)
- GET /api/quote/AAPL/historical (paginated historical OHLCV)
- GET /api/company/AAPL/historical-nocp (NOCP-specific history)
- GET /api/quote/AAPL/dividends (dividend history)
- GET /api/quote/basic (multi-symbol basic quotes, used for watchlists and key panels)
- GET /api/quote/COMP/info, /summary, and /chart for the COMP index

For finding instruments by name or ticker, the autocomplete search endpoint GET /api/autocomplete/slookup/10 is the key action-style endpoint, returning candidate symbols based on partial text such as 'A', 'Appl', or 'Apple'. This would be the primary entry point to automate symbol discovery before calling quote endpoints.

All of these market-data endpoints are simple GETs that accept query parameters (e.g., assetclass, date ranges, symbol lists) and return JSON. They are invoked by navigation page loads from www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/* pages, which themselves are HTML shells that rely on these APIs to fill in dynamic data.

No login, token refresh, or CSRF-fetch endpoints are present in this capture. The only explicit Authorization header appears on the /ai-search/external/indexer-api/clickstream/publish endpoint, which carries a Bearer JWT clearly intended for internal analytics/indexing rather than user-level auth. For routine construction, this endpoint is low-interest in terms of business logic but medium-interest as an example of how Nasdaq secures internal services.

The remainder of the traffic is dominated by consent-management and analytics infrastructure: OneTrust consent JSON and templates, Adobe smetrics /interact and /collect beacons, Marketo /webevents tracking, Qualtrics site intercept and session recording, Google CCM form-data posts, Bing /action and /actionp pixels, Reddit and LinkedIn pixels, JWPlayer playlist and tracking, and Akamai RUM /eum/results.txt. These endpoints are all categorized as low interest for automation, as they do not affect core user tasks.

In summary, the main API endpoint family needed for this task is the set of GET endpoints under https://api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/* and related historical/dividend/company paths, with /api/quote/AAPL/info and /api/quote/basic standing out as the most central for retrieving instrument details and basic quotes. The environment uses largely unauthenticated public GET access for market data, with heavy use of cookies and third-party analytics for tracking and personalization but no visible auth requirements for these data APIs in this capture.
